package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'electron' package and contains malicious code that collects sensitive user and device information (IP address, geolocation, username, home directory, CPU model) and exfiltrates it to a public GitHub issue via the GitHub API. This behavior is not expected in a legitimate package and results in public exposure of user data.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (preinstall), the package executes 'update.js' in the background, enabling the subsequent malicious data collection and exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Preinstall scripts are often abused to execute arbitrary code before the package is even installed, which can be used to compromise the environment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely use preinstall scripts, and when they do, they should not launch background processes unrelated to installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use preinstall for environment checks or setup, but not for background data collection.
key_indicators: Background execution of a script during installation
No legitimate installation logic in the script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code collects device fingerprinting information (username, home directory, CPU model, or machine ID) and encodes it in base64.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting device fingerprinting information is not required for normal package operation and is a privacy violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect or encode user and hardware information during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise software may fingerprint devices for licensing, but this is disclosed and not hidden.
key_indicators: Base64 encoding of user and hardware data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code queries an external IP geolocation service (ifconfig.co) to obtain the user's public IP address, country, and city.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching geolocation data is not required for normal package operation and is a privacy violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not contact external IP geolocation services during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or telemetry tools may fetch geolocation, but this is disclosed and opt-in.
key_indicators: Parsing and extracting IP, country, city

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code posts the collected device fingerprint and geolocation data to a public GitHub issue via the GitHub API, making the data publicly accessible.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive user and device data to a public GitHub issue is a clear privacy violation and data breach.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not exfiltrate user data to public endpoints, especially not to public GitHub issues.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for posting user device data to a public issue.
key_indicators: POST method with sensitive data in body

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
setInterval(update, 3600000); // For electorn (every hour)
// For loadyaml: setInterval(update, 1800000); // every 30 minutes
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the code schedules itself to re-execute every hour (electorn) or every 30 minutes (loadyaml), repeatedly collecting and exfiltrating user data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence and repeated exfiltration increase the risk and impact of the attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not persistently run background data collection after installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some updaters or telemetry agents may run periodically, but not for exfiltrating sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious package (typosquatting on 'electron' or 'loadyaml').
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers execution of update.js via preinstall script.

attack_chain.action: update.js collects device fingerprinting information (username, home directory, CPU model, machine ID).
update.js fetches the user's public IP address and geolocation data from ifconfig.co.
update.js posts the collected data to a public GitHub issue via the GitHub API.
update.js schedules itself to repeat the data collection and exfiltration every hour (electorn) or every 30 minutes (loadyaml).
attack_chain.leads_to: Continuous exfiltration and exposure of user data.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of background scripts via npm preinstall
Collection of device fingerprinting information (username, home directory, CPU model, machine ID)
Network requests to IP geolocation services (e.g., ifconfig.co/json)
Network requests to api.github.com with POST method and sensitive data in body
Persistence via setInterval for repeated execution
file_indicators: Presence of update.js with obfuscated or minified code
package.json with preinstall script launching background process
Base64-encoded strings representing URLs or API endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for preinstall scripts that launch background processes. Flag packages that collect device/user information or make network requests to external services (especially ifconfig.co or api.github.com) during installation. Look for base64-encoded URLs or endpoints in package scripts. Detect repeated background execution (setInterval) and exfiltration of data to public endpoints. Review package.json for suspicious scripts and dependencies.
